extracted.intended_audience: Recipients of Federal financial assistance (educational institutions), Title IX Coordinators, investigators, decision-makers, and school administrators responsible for Title IX grievance procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements for institutional grievance processes addressing allegations of sexual harassment under Title IX, covering notice, investigation, hearings, appeals, informal resolution, recordkeeping, and anti-retaliation obligations for K-12 and postsecondary institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary delay or extension for good cause (process requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Process that allows for the temporary delay of the grievance process or the limited extension of time frames for good cause with written notice to the complainant and the respondent of the delay or extension and the reasons for the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good cause may include considerations such as the absence of a party, a party's advisor, or a witness; concurrent law enforcement activity; or the need for language assistance or accommodation of disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range of possible disciplinary sanctions and remedies (policy content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the range of possible disciplinary sanctions and remedies or list the possible disciplinary sanctions and remedies that the recipient may implement following any determination of responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of evidence (policy must state and apply uniformly)
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether the standard of evidence to be used to determine responsibility is the preponderance of the evidence standard or the clear and convincing evidence standard, apply the same standard of evidence for formal complaints against students as for formal complaints against employees, including faculty, and apply the same standard of evidence to all formal complaints of sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recipient must explicitly choose and apply one of the two named standards uniformly across parties and complaint types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures and permissible bases for appeals (policy content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the procedures and permissible bases for the complainant and respondent to appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures (policy content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the range of supportive measures available to complainants and respondents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privileged information (prohibition unless waived)
rubrics_metrics.description: Not require, allow, rely upon, or otherwise use questions or evidence that constitute, or seek disclosure of, information protected under a legally recognized privilege, unless the person holding such privilege has waived the privilege.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of grievance process upon receipt of formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a formal complaint, a recipient must provide written notice to the parties who are known of the recipient's grievance process that complies with this section, including any informal resolution process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of allegations — sufficient details and rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice must include the allegations of sexual harassment potentially constituting sexual harassment under §106.30, including sufficient details known at the time and with sufficient time to prepare a response before any initial interview. Sufficient details include the identities of the parties involved (if known), the conduct allegedly constituting sexual harassment, and the date and location of the alleged incident (if known). The written notice must include a statement that the respondent is presumed not responsible, that determination is made at conclusion, inform parties they may have an advisor of their choice (may be an attorney), may inspect and review evidence, and must inform parties of any provision in the code of conduct that prohibits knowingly making false statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be provided to parties known upon receipt of formal complaint; gives parties time to prepare for initial interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of additional allegations discovered during investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: If, in the course of an investigation, the recipient decides to investigate allegations about the complainant or respondent that are not included in the initial notice, the recipient must provide notice of the additional allegations to the parties whose identities are known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory dismissal when allegations fall outside Title IX sexual harassment definition or jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: If the conduct alleged would not constitute sexual harassment as defined in §106.30 even if proved, did not occur in the recipient's education program or activity, or did not occur against a person in the United States, the recipient must dismiss the formal complaint with regard to that conduct for purposes of sexual harassment under Title IX or this part; such a dismissal does not preclude action under another provision of the recipient's code of conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissive dismissal criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient may dismiss the formal complaint or any allegations therein if at any time during the investigation or hearing: the complainant notifies the Title IX Coordinator in writing that they wish to withdraw the formal complaint or any allegations therein; the respondent is no longer enrolled or employed by the recipient; or specific circumstances prevent the recipient from gathering evidence sufficient to reach a determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of dismissal and reasons provided simultaneously
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon a dismissal required or permitted, the recipient must promptly send written notice of the dismissal and reason(s) therefor simultaneously to the parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of formal complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may consolidate formal complaints as to allegations of sexual harassment against more than one respondent, or by more than one complainant against one or more respondents, or by one party against the other party, where the allegations of sexual harassment arise out of the same facts or circumstances. Where multiple parties are involved, singular references include the plural as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof and evidence-gathering rests on recipient
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that the burden of proof and the burden of gathering evidence sufficient to reach a determination regarding responsibility rest on the recipient and not on the parties, provided that the recipient cannot access, consider, disclose, or otherwise use a party's treatment records made or maintained by a physician/psychiatrist/psychologist/other recognized professional or paraprofessional acting in that capacity, unless the recipient obtains that party's voluntary, written consent (or parent's consent if the party is not an 'eligible student').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipient must carry investigatory burdens; special protections for treatment records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity to present witnesses and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an equal opportunity for the parties to present witnesses, including fact and expert witnesses, and other inculpatory and exculpatory evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: No restriction on parties discussing allegations or gathering evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Not restrict the ability of either party to discuss the allegations under investigation or to gather and present relevant evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity to have others present, including advisors
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the parties with the same opportunities to have others present during any grievance proceeding, including the opportunity to be accompanied to any related meeting or proceeding by the advisor of their choice (who may be an attorney), and not limit the choice or presence of advisor for either party in any meeting or grievance proceeding; the recipient may establish restrictions regarding the extent to which the advisor may participate, so long as restrictions apply equally to both parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance written notice of meetings and hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide, to a party whose participation is invited or expected, written notice of the date, time, location, participants, and purpose of all hearings, investigative interviews, or other meetings, with sufficient time for the party to prepare to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal access to inspect and review evidence and 10-day response period
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide both parties an equal opportunity to inspect and review any evidence obtained as part of the investigation that is directly related to the allegations, including evidence the recipient does not intend to rely upon, so that each party can meaningfully respond prior to conclusion of the investigation. Prior to completion of the investigative report, send the evidence to each party and their advisor in electronic format or hard copy, and provide at least 10 days to submit a written response that the investigator will consider prior to completion of the investigative report. Make all such evidence available at any hearing so each party can refer to it during cross-examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes inculpatory and exculpatory evidence from any source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative report requirement and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Create an investigative report that fairly summarizes relevant evidence and, at least 10 days prior to a hearing (if a hearing is required) or other time of determination regarding responsibility, send the investigative report to each party and the party's advisor in electronic format or hard copy for review and written response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigative report must fairly summarize relevant evidence; parties have time to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live hearing requirement for postsecondary institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: For postsecondary institutions, the recipient's grievance process must provide for a live hearing in which the decision-maker(s) must permit each party's advisor to ask the other party and any witnesses all relevant questions and follow-up questions, including those challenging credibility. Cross-examination must be conducted directly, orally, and in real time by the party's advisor and never by a party personally. At a party's request the live hearing must allow parties to be in separate rooms with technology enabling simultaneous seeing and hearing. Only relevant cross-examination and other questions may be asked. The decision-maker(s) must first determine whether a question is relevant and explain any decision to exclude a question as not relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a party lacks an advisor at the live hearing, the recipient must provide, without fee, an advisor of the recipient's choice to conduct cross-examination. Hearings may be virtual. Recipients must create an audio or audiovisual recording or transcript and make it available to the parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on relevance of prior sexual behavior or predisposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions and evidence about the complainant's sexual predisposition or prior sexual behavior are not relevant, unless offered to prove that someone other than the respondent committed the conduct alleged, or if they concern specific incidents of the complainant's prior sexual behavior with respect to the respondent and are offered to prove consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies at hearings and in written-question processes; decision-maker must explain exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of statements from parties/witnesses who do not submit to cross-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party or witness does not submit to cross-examination at the live hearing, the decision-maker(s) must not rely on any statement of that party or witness in reaching a determination regarding responsibility; however, decision-maker(s) cannot draw an inference about responsibility based solely on a party's or witness's absence from the live hearing or refusal to answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative procedures for elementary and secondary schools (no required live hearing)
rubrics_metrics.description: For K-12 and other recipients that are not postsecondary institutions, the recipient's grievance process may, but need not, provide for a hearing. With or without a hearing, after the investigative report and before determining responsibility, the decision-maker(s) must afford each party the opportunity to submit written, relevant questions for any party or witness, provide each party with the answers, and allow for additional limited follow-up questions. The same rules on relevance and explanation of exclusions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-maker independence and standard of evidence for determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision-maker(s), who cannot be the same person(s) as the Title IX Coordinator or the investigator(s), must issue a written determination regarding responsibility, applying the standard of evidence described in policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of written determination regarding responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The written determination must include: (A) identification of the allegations potentially constituting sexual harassment; (B) a description of the procedural steps taken from receipt through determination, including notifications, interviews, site visits, evidence-gathering methods, and hearings held; (C) findings of fact supporting the determination; (D) conclusions regarding application of the recipient's code of conduct to the facts; (E) a statement of, and rationale for, the result as to each allegation including determination regarding responsibility, any disciplinary sanctions imposed, and whether remedies will be provided to restore or preserve equal access; and (F) the recipient's procedures and permissible bases for appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision and finality of written determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient must provide the written determination to the parties simultaneously. The determination becomes final either on the date the recipient provides the parties the written determination of the result of the appeal (if appeal filed), or if an appeal is not filed, the date on which an appeal would no longer be considered timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator responsibility for implementing remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Title IX Coordinator is responsible for effective implementation of any remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals: required bases to offer both parties
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must offer both parties an appeal from a determination regarding responsibility, and from a recipient's dismissal of a formal complaint or any allegations therein, on the following bases: (A) Procedural irregularity that affected the outcome; (B) New evidence that was not reasonably available at the time and that could affect the outcome; and (C) The Title IX Coordinator, investigator(s), or decision-maker(s) had a conflict of interest or bias for or against complainants or respondents generally or the individual party that affected the outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals: additional bases and equitable application
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may offer an appeal equally to both parties on additional bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals: procedural protections and decision requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For all appeals the recipient must: notify the other party in writing when an appeal is filed and implement appeal procedures equally; ensure appeal decision-maker(s) are not the same as prior decision-makers, investigators, or Title IX Coordinator; ensure appeal decision-maker(s) comply with applicable standards (e.g., impartiality); give both parties a reasonable, equal opportunity to submit a written statement in support of or challenging the outcome; issue a written decision describing the result and rationale; and provide the written decision simultaneously to both parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal resolution: voluntary and limited circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may not require waiver of the right to an investigation and adjudication as a condition of enrollment/employment or require participation in informal resolution. The recipient may facilitate an informal resolution process (e.g., mediation) at any time prior to reaching a determination regarding responsibility, provided that: (i) the recipient provides written notice disclosing the allegations and the requirements of the informal resolution process including circumstances under which it precludes resuming a formal complaint and consequences and records to be maintained/shared; (ii) obtains the parties' voluntary, written consent to the informal resolution; and (iii) does not offer or facilitate informal resolution for allegations that an employee sexually harassed a student.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties retain right to withdraw from informal resolution and resume grievance process prior to agreeing to a resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping — seven-year retention for investigations and trainings
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must maintain for seven years records of: each sexual harassment investigation including any determination regarding responsibility and any audio/audiovisual recording or transcript, any disciplinary sanctions imposed, and any remedies provided; any appeal and the result; any informal resolution and the result; and all materials used to train Title IX Coordinators, investigators, decision-makers, and any person who facilitates an informal resolution process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recipient must make these training materials publicly available on its website or available upon request if no website is maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping for responses under §106.44 — supportive measures and deliberate-indifference documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: For each response required under §106.44, a recipient must create and maintain for seven years records of any actions, including supportive measures, taken in response to a report or formal complaint. In each instance the recipient must document the basis for its conclusion that its response was not deliberately indifferent, and document that it has taken measures designed to restore or preserve equal access. If supportive measures were not provided, document reasons why such a response was not clearly unreasonable in light of the known circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation of certain bases/measures does not limit the recipient from providing additional explanations later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retaliation prohibited (substantive prohibition and confidentiality)
rubrics_metrics.description: No recipient or other person may intimidate, threaten, coerce, or discriminate against any individual for the purpose of interfering with any right or privilege secured by Title IX or because the individual has made a report, filed a complaint, testified, assisted, participated, or refused to participate in any manner in an investigation, proceeding, or hearing under this part. Intimidation/threats/coercion/discrimination that arise out of the same facts or circumstances as a report or complaint for the purpose of interfering with Title IX rights constitutes retaliation. The recipient must keep confidential the identity of any individual who has made a report or complaint, any complainant, any individual reported to be a perpetrator, any respondent, and any witness, except as permitted by FERPA or required by law or to carry out Title IX purposes (e.g., investigations/hearings). Complaints alleging retaliation may be filed according to grievance procedures for sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific exceptions — First Amendment and bad-faith false statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The exercise of rights protected under the First Amendment does not constitute retaliation. Charging an individual with a code of conduct violation for making a materially false statement in bad faith in the course of a grievance proceeding does not constitute retaliation, provided that a determination regarding responsibility alone is not sufficient to conclude that any party made a materially false statement in bad faith.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability of regulatory provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: If any provision of this subpart or its application to any person, act, or practice is held invalid, the remainder of the subpart or the application of its provisions to any person, act, or practice shall not be affected thereby.
